/ 01Diagnose the conveyor

What is the belt doing?

Six failure modes cause most conveyor downtime. Pick what you're seeing — it routes to an engineered fix, not a catalogue page.

01

Mistracking & wander

The belt drifts off its centre line and eats its own edges.

→ 02

Carryback & buildup

Material clings past discharge and lands where it shouldn't.

→ 03

Spillage & dust

Material escapes at transfer points into housekeeping and risk.

→ 04

Impact damage

Drop forces at loading hammer the belt and the structure.

→ 05

Rip & tear risk

A trapped object turns one metre of damage into a kilometre.

→ 06

Scale accuracy drift

/ 02The system

Five zones of control

01 / 05
01 Zone 01 — Load & transfer

Where problems begin.

Material drop forces damage the belt and misalign the load. Control impact and containment at the transfer point and the rest of the system inherits a stable belt.

Impact bedsSkirting & sealingDust control
Load-zone components

Stabilise after loading.

Mistracking wanders into spillage, edge damage and structural wear. Carry-side trackers and engineered idlers hold the belt centred at any tonnage.

Belt trackersIdlers & frames
Carry-side components

Carryback starts here.

Material that clings past the head pulley becomes buildup, spillage and housekeeping risk. Primary and secondary cleaners remove it at the source.

Primary cleanersSecondary cleaners
Discharge components

Protect the return run.

Whatever cleaning misses, the return-side spreads along the gantry. Return trackers and plows protect pulleys and keep the tail drift-free.

Return trackersV-plows
Return-side components

See it before it compounds.

Rip detection and belt scales convert the belt from a blind spot into a measured asset — catching the first failure before it cascades into the next.

Rip detectionBelt scales
Monitoring systems

From first call to running belt.

One accountable path — no hand-off between a sales desk and a fitter you've never met.

    Assess
